cost_estimate: Approximately 5 baseline tokenizer fits for replicas plus one final fit (about 6x Stage2 training compute); assignment alignment costs O(B*L*K^3), negligible at K=256 relative to fitting.
falsifiable_hypothesis: Across at least three seeds, consensus training reduces item assignment disagreement between independently fitted tokenizer seeds and improves validation next-item ranking versus the baseline at the same final-fit budget; if disagreement falls but validation ranking does not improve, discard.
key_change: Fit several lightweight tokenizer replicas on bootstrap resamples of training items, align replica code labels to a reference per codebook with Hungarian matching, then use cross-replica assignment frequencies as soft targets for a final standard tokenizer fit.
motivation: A small shift in initialization or sampled training items can move borderline products across code boundaries, making their semantic tokens unstable and depriving the generative recommender of repeatable prefix structure.
novelty: This targets tokenizer estimation uncertainty rather than adding another semantic modality, geometry, or sequential objective: train-only resampled tokenizer replicas estimate which item/code assignments are reliable, and only unstable assignments are regularized toward consensus.
risks: Code labels may not align cleanly where clusters split/merge; consensus can freeze a shared but poor local solution and reduce code utilization. Extra compute is substantial, and replica-derived targets can over-regularize rare items.

specification.text: Train B=5 replicas with the baseline architecture and hyperparameters, each sampling N training items with replacement and independent seed. For each level l, align replica code labels to replica 0 by maximum overlap of item assignments (Hungarian algorithm on the KxK overlap matrix). Define q_i,l,k=(1/B)sum_b 1[aligned_code_b(i,l)=k]. In the final tokenizer fit, retain the usual reconstruction/RQ loss and add L_cons=(gamma/(N*L))*sum_{i,l} KL(q_i,l || p_l(.|x_i)), where p is softmax of negative squared distances divided by fixed temperature tau=0.1 and gamma is selected from {0.01,0.1}; export the final model's ordinary hard assignments. All replicas and final fitting use training items only.

title: Assign IDs by bootstrap-consensus quantization
